label: Bible Study
prompt: The voice of him that crieth in the _____, Prepare ye the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.
verse: The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.
note: All four Gospels apply this voice to John the Baptist, preparing the way.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: For ye were as sheep going _____; but are now returned unto the Shepherd and Bishop of your souls.
verse: For ye were as sheep going astray; but are now returned unto the Shepherd and Bishop of your souls.
note: Once wandering sheep, now home with the Shepherd and Bishop of our souls.

label: Sunday School
prompt: That the waters which came down from above stood and rose up upon an _____ very far from the city Adam, that is beside Zaretan: and those that came down toward the sea of the plain, even the salt sea, failed, and were cut off: and the people passed over right against Jericho.
verse: That the waters which came down from above stood and rose up upon an heap very far from the city Adam, that is beside Zaretan: and those that came down toward the sea of the plain, even the salt sea, failed, and were cut off: and the people passed over right against Jericho.
note: When the priests' feet touched the Jordan, the river stood up in a heap far upstream — and Israel walked across.

label: Deep Water
prompt: So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem: for he did eat continually at the king's table; and was _____ on both his feet.
verse: So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem: for he did eat continually at the king's table; and was lame on both his feet.
note: David kept his vow to Jonathan by seating Jonathan's lame son at the royal table for life.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: How shall we escape, if we _____ so great salvation; which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed unto us by them that heard him;
verse: How shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation; which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed unto us by them that heard him;
note: Hebrews' first warning: the danger isn't rejecting so great salvation outright — it's simply to 'neglect' it.
